instructions: Elcano Pages hosts versioned, Flag-themed client dashboards at stable live URLs. Use list_workspaces and filtered list_pages to discover existing work before creating anything. deploy_page creates a missing page and publishes by default on open pages; update_page requires an existing page. Pass expected_version when updating a page you previously read. These tools are for small inline HTML only. For HTML saved in a workspace file or over 20,000 UTF-8 bytes, never paste the whole file into deploy_page/update_page and never pass a path, $(cat...), or placeholder. Compute the exact file byte count and lowercase SHA-256. If the client's append_page_upload schema accepts a workspace file reference, prefer start_page_upload then ordered append_page_upload calls with chunk_base64={workspace_file: relative_path, sha256: whole_file_sha256, offset: accepted_raw_bytes, length: next_raw_chunk_bytes}. The client reads and encodes exact bytes; do not print or transcribe base64. Use returned next_sequence and as few appends as returned max_chunk_bytes allows (make each length max_chunk_bytes until the last), then call deploy_page_upload. Otherwise prefer create_upload_ticket: PUT the file to the returned URL from your shell, then call deploy_page_upload with upload_id. If outbound HTTP is unavailable, use start_page_upload followed by ordered append_page_upload base64 chunks at returned next_sequence, as few appends as returned max_chunk_bytes allows, then the same consumer. Retry an interrupted append with the same sequence and bytes; do not cancel and restart unchanged content. Verify the returned byte count/hash before consuming the completed upload. Always follow page_is_live, version_is_live, live_version_id, and next_step. On approval-gated pages a new version waits for a human in urls.admin while an older published version may remain live. When an upload commit returns replayed:true, its version/revision, published, gated, and data fields are the original operation receipt; current live-state fields and next_step are refreshed without repeating that operation. Never infer current publication from published alone. Use create_workspace, rename_workspace, and set_page_workspace for reversible organization. Workspace deletion, approval/rejection, takedown controls, theme changes, password clearing, and restoration remain human-admin-only. Set a client password before sharing client-only work. delete_page is a reversible soft delete, but confirm with the user first. When a user says 'update <slug> dashboard with ...' or otherwise asks to change a specific existing dashboard, call prepare_dashboard_update first with that exact slug and the user's complete plain-language request. If an older static client allowlist hides that canonical tool, call its read-only compatibility alias configure_page_refresh with the same arguments. Use update_type=data for values only, layout for design/schema/JavaScript, or auto when classification is genuinely unclear. Never create a replacement slug or companion data page. For a one-time request, follow the returned prompt now in this conversation. If it returns migration_required, run that same-slug migration prompt, then call prepare_dashboard_update again as instructed. For recurring=true, show the returned prompt to the user verbatim so they can place it in their scheduler of choice; do not execute it now, claim that Pages scheduled it, or require Pages, MOC, Chat, Fleet, or Cutlass configuration changes. When following a managed-data prompt, call get_page_data with detail='summary' first and fetch the schema and rows once (detail='export' URLs downloaded to files where your client can, otherwise one full read), gather complete and fresh source data, map only the schema-defined data object, then call update_page_data with that live_version_id as expected_version and the latest represented source_as_of. Pages generates refreshed_at, preserves all layout/schema bytes, rejects source regressions, and dedupes exact retries. Never call the update when source data is missing, stale, or incomplete. After an ambiguous write or stale_version, reread once and compare schema/data hashes before at most one safe retry.
data_update_instructions: This token is restricted to Pages managed-data automation for exact granted slugs. Call get_page_data with detail='summary' first and use its live_version_id as update_page_data.expected_version. Read the schema and rows once per run: detail='export' returns short-lived URLs for a host-side download into files; detail='full' (the default) returns them inline. Gather every required source and enforce freshness/completeness before writing. Never guess, send credentials, or update partial/stale data. Map a complete data object against the returned self-contained JSON Schema. source_as_of is the latest represented source coverage; Pages separately generates refreshed_at. update_page_data preserves all layout and schema bytes, rejects regression/future coverage, serializes writers, and dedupes exact template+data+source retries. publish defaults true; publish:false creates a canary. On stale_version or an ambiguous write, reread and compare schema/data hashes, then retry at most once only if the intended source coverage is not already represented.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.title: List Pages
tools.description:
List active Pages with workspace, theme, client-access, serving state, and routing URLs. Supports bounded keyset pagination and filters; workspace_id:null selects Ungrouped.

Each row carries freshness: source_as_of, refreshed_at, checked_at, and days_since_* for each. That is how you find dashboards that have quietly stopped updating — Pages states no opinion on what counts as overdue, because it does not know any page's expected cadence.

refreshed_at.description: When that data was written to Pages.

tools.name: get_page_data
tools.title: Get Managed Page Data
tools.description:
Read the currently published managed-data contract. Use its live_version_id as update_page_data.expected_version. Fails with page_not_data_managed unless the published HTML has exactly one pages-data-schema block and one pages-data block.

detail picks how much comes back. 'summary' (~1–2 KB): brief page flags, live_version_id, the three hashes, envelope stamps, freshness and a coverage profile (per-array row counts, date field min/max/distinct, date-stamped scalars). Read it first; it is enough to decide whether a refresh is due. 'export': short-lived URLs for the schema, data and envelope of the live version, for a client that downloads URLs into workspace files host-side; the bytes then never enter your context, and sha256 of the schema/data files equals schema_sha256/data_sha256. 'full' (default): today's complete answer — schema, envelope with data, full data_profile, URLs and live state. Read the schema or rows once per run, by export where you can; do not re-read after a compaction.

freshness.source_as_of is the coverage watermark to compare your source against before refreshing: refresh when the source holds a period this page does not already represent, not because a file's timestamp moved.

detail.description: Default 'full'. 'summary' for the compact contract read; 'export' for download URLs instead of inline schema/data.

include_data.description: Full reads only. Default true. False returns the schema, hashes, profile, live state and coverage without envelope.data.

tools.name: get_page_refresh
tools.title: Get Dashboard Scheduling Guidance
tools.description: Compatibility read for clients that still ask about a Pages refresh. Pages no longer stores or dispatches recurring schedules. Read the exact existing page, then call prepare_dashboard_update—or configure_page_refresh on an older static allowlist—with the user's instructions and recurring=true. Show that returned prompt to the user for their own scheduler.

tools.name: record_refresh_check
tools.title: Record Refresh Check
tools.description:
Record that a refresh looked at this page and what it concluded, WITHOUT creating a version. Call it when a run ends without publishing — the source had no new coverage, a required tool was unavailable, a gate stopped it. It moves freshness.checked_at only: the published pointer, the data, and every hash are untouched, so the page keeps serving exactly what it was serving.

This is what separates a dashboard whose upstream has stopped producing from one nobody is running any more. Those look identical otherwise and need different people to act. A run that DID publish does not need this — update_page_data already stamps the page.

outcome.description: updated: a version was published. source_not_updated: the source held no coverage this page lacks. source_unreachable: the bound source could not be reached or authenticated. blocked: a gate stopped the run (schema drift, approval required, missing tool). failed: the run errored.

detail.description: One line a human can act on, e.g. 'upstream max date still 2026-07-02, unchanged for 6 days'.

source_as_of_seen.description: The latest coverage the SOURCE offered, when you could determine it. Compared against the page's own source_as_of, this is what shows an upstream has frozen rather than the job.

source_as_of.description: Latest source coverage the published data represents.

refreshed_at.description: When that data was written to Pages.

checked_at.description: Last time anyone LOOKED, whether or not it produced a version — max(refreshed_at, recorded check).

latest_outcome.description: Outcome at checked_at: updated when the live refresh is newer, otherwise the recorded check outcome.

last_check_outcome.description: Historical recorded check outcome at last_check_at, not necessarily the latest activity.

tools.name: prepare_dashboard_update
tools.title: Prepare Dashboard Update
tools.description: Prepare a safe exact-slug update prompt from a user's plain-language request. Call this whenever a user says 'update <slug> dashboard with ...'. For a one-time request, follow the returned prompt now. With recurring=true, the returned prompt is the verbatim task prompt of a recurring job (its cadence belongs to the job, not the prompt); Pages never schedules or dispatches it. update_type=data uses the managed-data contract, layout uses an existing-page staged deployment, and auto supplies bounded routing guidance. This tool is read-only and never changes a page.

instructions.description: The user's exact data/source/design request in plain language; describe credential locations, never secret values. For recurring=true describe the data work of one run (sources, scope, mappings, metrics), not when or how it is scheduled: scheduling and prompt-creation sentences are removed and echoed back as instructions_removed.

recurring.description: False/default: execute once now. True: return the task prompt for a recurring job; whoever schedules the job sets its cadence, and Pages does not schedule it.

update_type.description: Choose data for values only, layout for design/schema/JavaScript, or auto when the request genuinely needs classification.

publish.description: Whether the eventual update should publish; defaults true.

sources.description: Exact source bindings: which connector serves each input, where the data sits, and whether it is date-partitioned. REQUIRED when recurring is true — an unattended run executed weeks later cannot safely re-derive bindings from prose. Optional for a one-time update, but still the difference between a pinned source and a guess. Names only, never secret values.

source_id.description: Stable identifier for this input, e.g. ix_ssp or amazon_dsp.

mcp_server.description: MCP server name that serves it, e.g. indexexchange_mcp.

account.description: Logical connector account/variant name; omit for the default seat.

required_tools.description: Read-only tool names this source must be retrieved through.

path.description: Exact location in the source system, e.g. northwind/contoso/daily. Beats searching for a filename.

partition.description: Set when this source is a date-partitioned folder (one file per day). The prompt then requires enumerating EVERY partition in range — the default newest-wins pick silently publishes a single day of a multi-week dataset.

by.description: Only date partitioning is modelled today.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound, or source_as_of to continue from the page.

until.description: Inclusive upper bound; omit for the newest available.

retrieval_instructions.description: Deterministic, bounded retrieval detail for this source (window, filters, expected artifacts).

completion.description: Recurring managed data only: the run is complete when any one of these tools succeeded: a committed version or a recorded check.

blocked_when.description: The run finished without publishing when its last successful call of `tool` had `argument` set to one of `in` and no other completion tool succeeded; `detail_argument` names that call's argument holding the reason.

tools.name: find_in_version
tools.title: Find In Page Version
tools.description: Literal (non-regex) search inside a stored version, returning bounded line numbers and short excerpts instead of the document. Use this to locate the exact anchor text for patch_page without reading a whole dashboard back into context. Defaults to the published version. Read-only.

query.description: Exact substring to look for; not a regular expression.

version_id.description: Defaults to the currently published version.

tools.name: patch_page
tools.title: Patch Page
tools.description: Deploy a new version by applying small anchored find/replace edits to the CURRENT published HTML, server-side. Use this for targeted changes — a CSS rule, a handler name, a label — instead of re-uploading the whole document. `find` is a literal string, not a regex, and must match exactly `count` times (default 1) or the whole patch is rejected. Locate anchors with find_in_version. By default it patches the live version and is concurrency-checked against the live pointer, so a patch cannot clobber a deploy that landed between the read and the write. `base_version_id` patches a DIFFERENT version instead — and publishing that republishes its bytes, discarding whatever was deployed since, so pass `expected_version` (or `publish:false`) when you rebase off an older version deliberately.

find.description: Exact literal text to replace, whitespace included.

count.description: Required number of occurrences; defaults to 1.

edits.description: Applied in order; each sees the result of the previous.

base_version_id.description: Patch this version instead of the published one.

render_mode.description: Defaults to the base version's mode.

publish.description: Publish immediately on open pages; defaults to true.

expected_version.description: Defaults to the page's current live version, not to base_version_id.

live.description: Compatibility alias for version_is_live.

admin.description: Elcano-staff admin screen for this page (SSO, staff only).

view.description: Elcano-staff shortcut that opens the live page without its client password. Staff only — do NOT share this with a client; give them `live`.

live.description: The client link. Share this one; a password-protected page prompts for its password here.

config_schema_generated.description: Present only when this page shipped a #pages-config block with no #pages-config-schema, so Pages derived one from the values and wrote it into the stored document. It pins types and rejects unknown keys; it does not know your enums, formats or which keys are genuinely optional. Replace it by hand if this design becomes a family.

preflight.description: Static check of the deployed document against the content host's CSP and sandbox. Advisory only — the deploy already happened. Errors mean parts of the page will not work in a browser.

ok.description: True when no errors were found. Warnings do not clear it.

The managed-data contract error code, on managed_block_invalid.

tools.description: Check a stored version against the exact CSP and sandbox the content host serves it under, WITHOUT pulling the HTML into context. Reports controls that will silently do nothing in a browser: inline on*= handlers shadowed by a built-in DOM member, subresources the CSP blocks, APIs the sandbox ignores, and scripts that do not parse. Defaults to the published version. Read-only.

Read the workflow section for the step you are on before creating, reusing or changing a page; it does not replace your deployment's own rules on sources, approvals and access. Read-only; the text matches this server's version.

tools.name: create_upload_ticket
tools.title: Create Page Upload Ticket
tools.description: Managed-data limits in UTF-8 bytes: compact payload 1048576; stored HTML-escaped envelope 1048576 including timestamps and at least 114 metadata bytes; inline payload transport 1500000; staged raw file 2097152; complete JSON HTTP request 2097152 including RPC fields and expect. All applicable limits must fit. Direct file staging removes the file from inline/JSON-RPC transport budgets, never the data/envelope limits. Before staging kind='data', optionally supply advisory data_size: payload_bytes is UTF-8 byteLength(JSON.stringify(data)); escaped_payload_bytes counts the same JSON after replacing <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 with six-character Unicode escapes. Measure the parsed object, not pretty-printed file bytes; total_bytes and SHA-256 still describe the exact file. The server validates received content independently; measurements do not guarantee acceptance. For clients without workspace file references on append_page_upload, the preferred way to publish a file you already have on disk — page HTML, a template, or a managed-data JSON payload. Returns a one-shot URL your shell can PUT the file to directly, so the bytes never pass through your own output: `curl -fsS -X PUT --data-binary @<file> -H "Authorization: Bearer <ticket>" <upload_url>`. Supply the exact byte count and lowercase SHA-256 first — the ticket only ever accepts those exact bytes. Then call deploy_page_upload with the upload_id — register_template_upload if you staged a template, update_page_data_upload if you staged kind 'data'. Use append_page_upload instead only if your environment cannot make outbound HTTP requests.

slug.description: The page this upload targets. Supply exactly one of slug or template.

template.description: Register a reusable template instead of deploying a page. Consume with register_template_upload.

kind.description: With a slug: 'page' (default) stages HTML for deploy_page_upload; 'data' stages a managed-data JSON payload for update_page_data_upload. Fixed here and enforced at deploy, so JSON can never be served as a page and a document can never be parsed into a data envelope.

data_size.description: Advisory UTF-8 sizes of compact JSON and HTML-escaped compact JSON; only for kind data. Actual content is always validated.

content_sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the exact original UTF-8 file bytes.

upload_id.description: Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.

upload_url.description: PUT the raw file bytes here. Absolute — do not rebuild it from a hostname.

ticket.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <ticket>`. Write-only, single upload, expires in minutes.

curl.description: A ready-to-run command; substitute your local file path.

tools.name: start_page_upload
tools.title: Start Page Content Upload
tools.description: Managed-data limits in UTF-8 bytes: compact payload 1048576; stored HTML-escaped envelope 1048576 including timestamps and at least 114 metadata bytes; inline payload transport 1500000; staged raw file 2097152; complete JSON HTTP request 2097152 including RPC fields and expect. All applicable limits must fit. Direct file staging removes the file from inline/JSON-RPC transport budgets, never the data/envelope limits. Before staging kind='data', optionally supply advisory data_size: payload_bytes is UTF-8 byteLength(JSON.stringify(data)); escaped_payload_bytes counts the same JSON after replacing <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 with six-character Unicode escapes. Measure the parsed object, not pretty-printed file bytes; total_bytes and SHA-256 still describe the exact file. The server validates received content independently; measurements do not guarantee acceptance. Stage exact file bytes for ordered MCP appends. Prefer this path when your client advertises workspace_file references on append_page_upload.chunk_base64: the client reads and encodes the file, with no model-generated base64 and no shell credential. Supply the exact whole-file byte count and lowercase SHA-256, append the original bytes in sequence in as few appends as the returned max_chunk_bytes allows, then call the matching upload consumer. Staging does not publish. An append failure does not advance the sequence; retry the same exact bytes. Do not cancel and restart a usable upload. Clients without file-reference support need another permitted programmatic transport; create_upload_ticket supports direct file HTTP. Never print or transcribe a large base64 payload through model output.

slug.description: The page this upload targets. Supply exactly one of slug or template.

template.description: Register a reusable template instead of deploying a page. Consume with register_template_upload.

kind.description: With a slug: 'page' (default) stages HTML for deploy_page_upload; 'data' stages a managed-data JSON payload for update_page_data_upload.

data_size.description: Advisory UTF-8 sizes of compact JSON and HTML-escaped compact JSON; only for kind data. Actual content is always validated.

content_sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the exact original UTF-8 file bytes.

upload_id.description: Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.

tools.name: append_page_upload
tools.title: Append Page Content Upload
tools.description:
Append one ordered base64 chunk to a staged upload. If your client advertises a workspace_file reference for chunk_base64, use it to transmit exact file bytes without printing or generating base64. Decode size must not exceed max_chunk_bytes from start_page_upload; each append is a full round trip, so use as few appends as max_chunk_bytes allows. Send the exact next_sequence; replaying the same sequence and the same bytes is a safe no-op.

A FAILED append does not advance the sequence and does not lose anything already accepted, so every error here is resumable: re-send from the expected_sequence the error reports. Do not cancel to recover — that deletes every byte you have already emitted and makes you send the whole document again, which is how a single page can consume a whole turn.

Preserve original byte order; do not minify or alter content between chunks.

upload_id.description: Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.

chunk_base64.description: Canonical base64 for the next raw file chunk; no data-URI prefix or whitespace.

upload_id.description: Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.

tools.name: cancel_page_upload
tools.title: Cancel Page Content Upload
tools.description:
Discard an uncommitted staged upload and free its active-upload slot. This never changes a page or deployed version. Repeating a cancellation is a safe no-op; committed uploads cannot be cancelled.

Do NOT use this to recover from an append error. Sequence and hash failures are resumable — the failed chunk was not accepted and everything before it is still stored — so cancelling only throws away bytes you already paid to emit and forces the whole document again. Cancel when you no longer want to deploy this content at all.

upload_id.description: Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.
Opaque upload handle returned by start_page_upload.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.title: List Templates
tools.description: List reusable page templates: name, title, current revision, schema hashes, and how many pages were built from each. page_count is every live page whose history touches the design; serving_count is those whose PUBLISHED version still comes from it; drifted_count is the difference — pages a later raw deploy detached, which a design fix will no longer reach. Call list_template_pages to see which. A template is one stored design; a page built from it carries only its own config and data, so building the second dashboard of a family costs kilobytes of JSON instead of the whole document.

tools.name: get_template
tools.title: Get Template
tools.description: Read what a template needs in order to build a page: its config JSON Schema, its data JSON Schema, and the reference config it ships with. Call this INSTEAD of reading a dashboard's HTML — it answers 'what does this design require?' in a couple of KB. The HTML is omitted unless include_html is true, and you almost never need it. Pass revision to inspect an exact past revision.

template.description: Template name, for example 'nwm-campaign-dashboard'. No slashes.

include_html.description: Defaults to false. Only set this if you must edit the design itself.

reference_config.description: The config this template shipped with. A STARTING POINT to read, not a default to inherit: create_page_from_template requires a complete config so one client's identity can never leak into another's page.

tools.name: list_template_revisions
tools.title: List Template Revisions
tools.description: List a template's revisions, newest first, marking the current one. Pages pin the exact revision they were built from, so a new revision never changes a deployed page.

template.description: Template name, for example 'nwm-campaign-dashboard'. No slashes.

tools.name: create_template_from_page
tools.title: Make An Existing Page Reusable
tools.description: Promote a page you already like into a reusable design, WITHOUT moving its bytes — the design is already on the server, so nothing is re-authored and nothing passes through your output. Use this whenever someone says 'I want more pages like this one'. It requires only that the page already separates its per-instance values into a #pages-config block; if it does not, this fails with page_not_template_managed and you should separate them and redeploy first (a config schema is derived for you, so that costs no schema authoring). Then build the next client's page with create_page_from_template and a few KB of config.

tools.name: rerender_page_from_template

tools.description: Move ONE page onto a different revision of its template, or pull a DRIFTED page back onto it, keeping its own config and data by default. For a schema migration, supply complete target-valid config and/or data in this same call, with expected_version. Replacement data requires explicit source_as_of and records a fresh ingestion; omitted data preserves the entire live envelope. A page a raw deploy_page or patch_page detached (list_template_pages: drifted:true) has no binding left to infer the design from, so name the template explicitly and it is re-attached — which works as long as its published HTML still carries #pages-config and #pages-data, the usual case after patch_page. tools.name: update_page_data_upload
tools.title: Update Managed Page Data From Staged Upload
tools.description:
Managed-data limits in UTF-8 bytes: compact payload 1048576; stored HTML-escaped envelope 1048576 including timestamps and at least 114 metadata bytes; inline payload transport 1500000; staged raw file 2097152; complete JSON HTTP request 2097152 including RPC fields and expect. All applicable limits must fit. Direct file staging removes the file from inline/JSON-RPC transport budgets, never the data/envelope limits. Before staging kind='data', optionally supply advisory data_size: payload_bytes is UTF-8 byteLength(JSON.stringify(data)); escaped_payload_bytes counts the same JSON after replacing <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 with six-character Unicode escapes. Measure the parsed object, not pretty-printed file bytes; total_bytes and SHA-256 still describe the exact file. The server validates received content independently; measurements do not guarantee acceptance. Publish a managed-data payload you staged with create_upload_ticket (kind 'data') instead of sending it inline. The JSON never passes through your context. Payload, escaped-envelope and staged-file limits still apply. Everything else is update_page_data exactly: same schema validation, same monotonic source_as_of, same mandatory expected_version, same dedupe, same data_profile / data_warnings, same expect reconciliation — one write path, not two.

The staged bytes must parse as a JSON object. An upload staged as 'page' is refused here, and one staged as 'data' is refused by deploy_page_upload. Exact committed retries add replayed:true, preserve the original data receipt, and refresh current live-state fields and next_step without updating data again.

Use returned next_sequence and as few appends as returned max_chunk_bytes allows (make each length max_chunk_bytes until the last), then call deploy_page_upload. Otherwise prefer create_upload_ticket: PUT the file to the returned URL from your shell, then call deploy_page_upload with upload_id. If outbound HTTP is unavailable, use start_page_upload followed by ordered append_page_upload base64 chunks at returned next_sequence, as few appends as returned max_chunk_bytes allows, then the same consumer. Retry an interrupted append with the same sequence and bytes; do not cancel and restart unchanged content. Verify the returned byte count/hash before consuming the completed upload.

tools.name: update_page_data
tools.title: Update Managed Page Data
tools.description:
Validate structured data against the published page's embedded JSON Schema, then create an immutable version by replacing only the pages-data script contents. source_as_of is required, monotonic RFC3339 source coverage; refreshed_at is generated by Pages. expected_version is mandatory optimistic concurrency. Same template+data+source dedupes; newer source coverage versions even unchanged metrics. Defaults publish=true; use publish=false for a canary.

The schema validates SHAPE ONLY — a payload missing three weeks of days, or a whole deal, satisfies it exactly as well as a correct one. So the response returns data_profile (row counts, date extents, numeric totals, distinct values of low-cardinality keys) and data_warnings (coverage that starts later or ends earlier than what is already published, rows that dropped, dimension values that disappeared). RECONCILE data_profile against your source before you tell anyone the page is right. Better: pass expect with the totals you computed from the source and let Pages refuse the write if the payload disagrees.

data.description: Complete data object that satisfies the page's returned schema; never include credentials. SEND IT WHOLE. Do not split it across calls, sample it, or decline to send because it looks large. Managed-data limits in UTF-8 bytes: compact payload 1048576; stored HTML-escaped envelope 1048576 including timestamps and at least 114 metadata bytes; inline payload transport 1500000; staged raw file 2097152; complete JSON HTTP request 2097152 including RPC fields and expect. All applicable limits must fit. Direct file staging removes the file from inline/JSON-RPC transport budgets, never the data/envelope limits. Before staging kind='data', optionally supply advisory data_size: payload_bytes is UTF-8 byteLength(JSON.stringify(data)); escaped_payload_bytes counts the same JSON after replacing <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 with six-character Unicode escapes. Measure the parsed object, not pretty-printed file bytes; total_bytes and SHA-256 still describe the exact file. The server validates received content independently; measurements do not guarantee acceptance. Compute the exact file byte count and lowercase SHA-256. If the client's append_page_upload schema accepts a workspace file reference, prefer start_page_upload kind='data' then ordered append_page_upload calls with chunk_base64={workspace_file: relative_path, sha256: whole_file_sha256, offset: accepted_raw_bytes, length: next_raw_chunk_bytes}. The client reads and encodes exact bytes; do not print or transcribe base64. Use returned next_sequence and as few appends as returned max_chunk_bytes allows (make each length max_chunk_bytes until the last), then call update_page_data_upload. Otherwise prefer create_upload_ticket kind='data': PUT the file to the returned URL from your shell, then call update_page_data_upload with upload_id. A partial payload passes schema validation while publishing wrong numbers. On those clients call this whenever a user says 'update <slug> dashboard with ...', passing the exact request as instructions. It is read-only: Pages does not configure, persist, or dispatch a schedule. A legacy workflow argument is converted into recurring prompt text and daily_at_utc is accepted but not written into it, so already-deployed clients need no code change; run_now never executes work.

instructions.description: Preferred: the user's exact plain-language request.

daily_at_utc.description: Legacy compatibility only; Pages does not install this cadence.

workflow.description: Legacy credential-free source workflow converted into user-owned prompt text.

run_now.description: Legacy compatibility only; ignored because prompt preparation never executes work.

source_id.description: Stable identifier for this input, e.g. ix_ssp or amazon_dsp.

mcp_server.description: MCP server name that serves it, e.g. indexexchange_mcp.

account.description: Logical connector account/variant name; omit for the default seat.

required_tools.description: Read-only tool names this source must be retrieved through.

path.description: Exact location in the source system, e.g. northwind/contoso/daily. Beats searching for a filename.

partition.description: Set when this source is a date-partitioned folder (one file per day). The prompt then requires enumerating EVERY partition in range — the default newest-wins pick silently publishes a single day of a multi-week dataset.

by.description: Only date partitioning is modelled today.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound, or source_as_of to continue from the page.

until.description: Inclusive upper bound; omit for the newest available.

retrieval_instructions.description: Deterministic, bounded retrieval detail for this source (window, filters, expected artifacts).

instructions_removed.description: Recurring only: scheduling and prompt-creation prose removed from instructions before quoting them as USER REQUEST.

roster.description: Recurring managed data with fully bound sources only: offer the run only required_tools; every tool a branch may call is listed.

completion.description: Recurring managed data only: the run is complete when any one of these tools succeeded: a committed version or a recorded check.

blocked_when.description: The run finished without publishing when its last successful call of `tool` had `argument` set to one of `in` and no other completion tool succeeded; `detail_argument` names that call's argument holding the reason.

serialization_key.description: pages:<slug>. Runs sharing it should not overlap; give every schedule for this page the same key.
